answer.rationale: The two metrics that actually moved are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the competitor's pricing is a separate, louder signal that tempts an expensive response. Two inherited memories (memory_86, memory_31) point at the funnel stage where the loss is observable, so that is where the single slot buys the most durable qualified revenue. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the intended action and I want to know what 'shortening' concretely meant (which steps were cut, whether the lift persisted past week one, and whether completion gains actually converted to retained revenue rather than just faster tourists). I am verifying memory_73 because it is the strongest pull toward promotional_pricing and it carries an explicit methodological caveat: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real effect. If that record turns out clean and the segment definition holds, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender; if it is as compromised as the note suggests, I should not spend the only slot chasing it, and discounting into a price war would likely buy low-margin, high-churn accounts that reduce sustainable qualified revenue even while headline acquisition looks good. Downstream value risk on my own chosen action: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on sales-assisted routing, which needs exactly those qualification fields. Blindly stripping fields could lift SMB activation while quietly degrading enterprise lead routing and net qualified revenue. So I will scope the test to the self-serve SMB path where the prior evidence actually lives, leave the demo-request path untouched, and instrument downstream qualified-revenue and 30/60-day retention rather than stopping at completion rate. memory_91 (activation messaging) remains the fallback if verification shows the onboarding lift was thin or non-durable, since it targets the same activation deficit with a lighter footprint. I am not treating any of these memories as settled fact: they are archived consolidations, the caveat on memory_73 shows this record can carry known defects, and none of them were measured against a competitor-pricing shock, so effect sizes may not transfer to day 76 conditions.
